findings.title: Fallback locales are loaded only for controller requests
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` lazy-loads only the current locale via `load_locale(config.locale)`, so translations performed outside controller actions (for example mailers, background jobs, or rake tasks) with a non-default locale will not have the site-default or `:en` YAML loaded before fallback lookup runs. A missing key in the current locale can then fail or produce an I18n missing-translation error instead of falling back. The fallback preloading must happen wherever `I18n.locale` is set, or `translate` should load the fallback chain itself.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The cached translation key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, a translation that is missing in the requested locale can be resolved from a fallback locale and then cached under the requested locale. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes at runtime, the same key and locale would need a different fallback resolution, but the old cached value is still returned until `I18n.reload!` clears the cache. This can serve stale translations after an admin changes the default locale. Include the fallback chain in the cache key or invalidate the translation cache when the default locale changes.

findings.title: No tests cover the new fallback behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces a custom fallback order, loads fallbacks and pluralization in a new initializer, removes environment-specific fallback flags, and adds `ensure_loaded!` wiring, but no specs are added. The behavior should be tested: anonymous users use the site default, logged-in users fall back in the expected order, fallback locale YAMLs are actually loaded, and non-controller translation paths do not regress. Without tests, this lazy-loading/fallback interaction is easy to break.
